_comment: The archive path rules ported from staged-product-inputs.ts. Every trial here removes one refusal, and the test that dies is the attack that refusal exists for. This is path-traversal defence over untrusted input, so a survivor means a door left open rather than a metric left unmeasured. One trial was removed rather than fixed: 'an absolute path is accepted'. Measured, not assumed — an absolute path always splits to a leading empty component, so the component rule refuses every shape of one on its own. The check stays and the reason is recorded at it, the same treatment sm_alloc's max(len,1) gets.
verify: scripts/dev-shell.sh cargo test -q -p xtask --target "$(rustc -vV | sed -n 's/^host: //p')" archive_paths >/dev/null 2>&1

trials.name: a directory entry's trailing slash is not dropped
a root with nothing beneath it is accepted
an archive with two top-level directories is accepted
stripping does not re-check the root it strips
a link inside an archive is planned rather than refused
an unexpected top-level directory is accepted
an expected root is silently ignored when nothing computes one
